newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsang concerned at rising land prices, inflation.
newsitem.headline: Tsang concerned at rising land prices, inflation.

text.p: Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said he would chair a special task force on land supply, and expressed concern over rising property prices and inflation.
Presenting a budget on Wednesday, Tsang predicted Hong Kong's inflation in the 1997/98 fiscal year would rise to seven percent, and warned of pressures on land resources.
"Indeed we have already seen pressures building up faster than we would prefer on the property market in particular," he said.
According to background documents tabled with the budget, demand for flats in selected residential developments topped previous peak levels of April 1994.
According to the documents, the price fetched for one site sold by the government was the highest ever achieved for a single site at a government auction.
Tsang said housing demand still outstripped supply, hence a decision to make 46 percent more land available over the next five years for residential housing.
"But I recognise that we must try to do even more," Tsang said. "So, I have decided to chair a special task force to look at land supply and its impact on infrastructure and housing development."
He said the Inland Revenue Department was already charging profits tax on any gains made by speculators using companies to buy flats then reselling them shortly afterwards.

The government also planned to step up efforts to help Hong Kong people own their own homes, and expected to provide loans for a further 3,000 families as a result of a recent decision to inject HK$1.38 billion into a loan scheme, he said.
